sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Function verb phrases and nominal structures make professional German dense — and sometimes hard to read.

blocks.text: A Funktionsverbgefüge pairs a noun with a light verb: zur Anwendung kommen, in Betracht ziehen, zur Verfügung stellen, in Frage stellen. The verb carries little meaning; the noun carries the content. These phrases are common in official and academic German.

They are useful when you need a formal, impersonal tone. They become a problem when they replace a clear verb for no reason. “Die Maßnahme kommt zur Anwendung” is more formal than “Die Maßnahme wird angewendet”, but not always better. Choose based on register and clarity.

blocks.title: Prefer the clear verb unless register demands otherwise
blocks.text: In a report, “Wir prüfen den Vorschlag” is usually better than “Wir ziehen den Vorschlag in Betracht”. Use the nominal phrase when it adds precision or the right level of formality.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Die Maßnahme kommt nur unter bestimmten Bedingungen zur Anwendung.
Wir ziehen auch andere Lösungen in Betracht.
Das Unternehmen stellt die Daten zur Verfügung.
Die Ergebnisse stellen die bisherige Annahme in Frage.

items: These phrases often use a prepositional phrase with zu or in.
The noun is usually feminine or neuter and takes a fixed article.
Do not stack three function verb phrases in one sentence.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The ch is soft: in be-TRACHT.
Stress the second word: tsur fer-FOO-gung.

blocks.text: Function verb phrases are a hallmark of German administrative and academic language. They signal formality and distance, which is appropriate in reports and official letters.
Plain-language movements in Germany and Austria push for clearer official texts. The goal is not to ban these phrases, but to use them only when they help.

lines.en: Does this sentence sound too colloquial?

lines.speaker: Kollege
lines.de: Ja. Statt „wir nutzen die Methode“ schreiben wir „die Methode kommt zur Anwendung“.
lines.en: Yes. Instead of “we use the method”, we write “the method is applied”.

lines.speaker: Kollegin
lines.de: Und was machen wir mit dem Vorschlag?
lines.en: And what do we do with the proposal?

lines.speaker: Kollege
lines.de: Wir ziehen ihn in Betracht, stellen ihn aber nicht in Frage.
lines.en: We consider it, but we do not call it into question.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Function verb phrases
sections.lede: Noun + light verb: formal, impersonal, often replaceable by a single verb.

blocks.text: The noun in a function verb phrase is usually fixed. You cannot replace Anwendung with Nutzung without changing the expression. Learn the whole phrase.

sections.tip: If a sentence contains three function verb phrases, replace one with a plain verb. The text will be clearer without losing formality.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Rewrite two plain sentences in formal style using function verb phrases, then explain one drawback.

model.de: Statt „wir nutzen die Methode“ schreibe ich „die Methode kommt zur Anwendung“. Statt „wir prüfen den Vorschlag“ schreibe ich „wir ziehen den Vorschlag in Betracht“. Das klingt formeller, kann aber unklar wirken.
model.en: Instead of “we use the method”, I write “the method is applied”. Instead of “we check the proposal”, I write “we consider the proposal”. That sounds more formal but can seem unclear.

tips: Keep the noun fixed: Anwendung, Betracht, Verfügung, Frage.
Use function verb phrases once or twice, not in every sentence.
Say why the formal version might be less clear.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.wrong: Wir ziehen andere Lösungen in Betracht ziehen.
items.right: Wir ziehen andere Lösungen in Betracht.
items.why: Do not repeat the infinitive in the main clause.

items.wrong: Die Ergebnisse stellen die Annahme in Frage stellen.
items.right: Die Ergebnisse stellen die Annahme in Frage.
items.why: The separable prefix Frage closes the sentence; no second verb is needed.
